newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose against the dollar in quiet trading on Wednesday following an unexpectedly high June consumer price index (CPI), dealers said.
The June CPI, released after the representative rate was set on Tuesday, rose 1.1 percent, well above expectations of a rise of 0.5 percent to 0.8 percent.
"It is now clear that the Bank of Israel will not lower its key lending rate at the end of the month. It may even decide to raise rates," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank.
Nevertheless, she said, the market continued to be very quiet.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5560 shekels against 3.5670 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.8337 against 3.8482 on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.0723 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.1196 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 1.9851 shekels compared with 1.9870 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5540 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
